scope: Narrowing the remaining organic clock-slot probe around the live Select Opponent callback window.

claim_audit.claim: Absolute-frame input windows remain unstable for the fourth-slot clock probe because delaying confirmation also shifts the first live 01:C1D2 window later, leaving right+down early in both bounded follow-ups.
evidence: tools/out/select_opponent_clock_path_v3/td2_boot_probe.json reaches c20b at frame 1600 and first c1d2 only at 1615..1617; the right+down window 1600..1605 therefore still lands before the live callback.
The same v3 run still falls through the default path, reaching be76 at 1616, b87 at 1706, 902d at 1857, and first active_main = 02:9016 at 2014 with $1C70 unchanged at 0.

tools/out/select_opponent_clock_path_v4/td2_boot_probe.json reaches c20b at frame 1613 and first c1d2 only at 1628..1637; the delayed right+down window 1620..1625 is still early relative to the live callback.

In v4, delayed start at 1630..1635 does reach be76 at 1636, but no b87 or 902d hit appears through the 1450..1900 trace window, and sampled later frames stay on active_main = 01:BE43 with $1C70 still 0.
claim_audit.notes: The remaining clock-slot problem is now better described as callback-relative timing drift, not a raw button-map question. The next defensible probe should overlap right+down with the live C1D2 window itself or trigger relative to first C1D2 rather than fixed absolute frames.

scenarios.notes: The run still closes the default-rival baseline because right+down lands before C1D2 becomes live.
Delaying confirmation shifts the live C1D2 window later instead of creating a stable absolute-frame target.

next_gate: Use an overlapping or callback-relative right+down injection so the fourth-slot move is guaranteed to occur while 01:C1D2 is already live.
